lawyer:
Abdur Razaque Khan, Additional Attorney-General, (Golam Mohammad Chowdhury, Deputy Attorney- General with him) instructed by Sufia Khatun, Advocate-on-Record------ For the State Appellant. 
Zainal Abedin, Senior Advocate, (Nitai Roy Chowdhury, Advocate with him) instructed by Abu Siddique, Advocate-on-Record------ For the Respondent.
parties:
State ------ Appellant 
vs.
Wasikur Rahman and another ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
"Mr Shafiuddin, the learned Deputy Attorney-General, submits that in rejecting the evidence of PWs 1,2, 3 and 4 the High Court Division has violated and trampled on the accepted and well established forms of appreciation of evidence and has found insignificant immaterial and trivial omissions to be material discrepancies in their respective evidence. The eye- witnesses were disbelieved by comparing their testimony with the statements made in the first information report by PW 1 who was not an eye-witness himself. The rejection of evidence of eye-witnesses to the occurrence on such flimsy and inconsequential grounds has caused a grave failure of justice and also a miscarriage of justice inasmuch as a gruesome murder witnessed by three eye-witnesses has gone unpunished in the face of unimpeachable eye-witness evidence on record. The High Court Division also illegally took into consideration the evidence of PW 17 as a substantive piece of evidence on the manner of occurrence, because PW 17 was not an eye-witness. The High Court Division commented about the enmity between the informant party and the accused respondents and most illegally drew the inference in favour of the defence by inventing doubt because of enmity. He further submits that the question of recognition does not arise because the occurrence took place before a Cinema Hall in the evening where electric lights lighted the place of occurrence and, particularly when the defence did not raise any question of recognition. Again, the question of examining any person of the Cinema Hall or any other shopkeeper does not arise because there is no evidence that any of them saw the occurrence. The fact that there is no evidence as to who brought the dead body of TutuI from the Cinema Hall to the hospital is also of no consequence. The High Court Division was totally in error of law in finding misreading of evidence without pointing out where the misreading by the trial Court has taken place. The disposal of the appeal in the manner in which it has been done has resulted in a travesty of justice and the evidence needs to be gone into afresh." 

 4. Mr Abdur Razaque Khan, learned Additional Attorney-General in support of the appeal, submits, inter alia, that there is, in fact, no discrepancy in the evidence of three eye-witnesses PWs 2, 3 and 4 and, as such, the High Court Division, committed error of law in rejecting the death reference. 

 6. He further submits with reference to the first information report and the evidence of witnesses that the allegation that Moshfequr, Rahman caught hold of the victim Tutul cannot be brushed aside in view of cogent evidence of the witnesses and, in fact, there is no departure in the evidence of witnesses from the first information report in this respect and that though in evidence it appears that there were some other persons too catching hold of the victim but the fact remains that Moshfequr Rahman was one of them to catch hold of the victim. 

 7. He emphatically submits that so far as Wasikur Rahman is concerned the evidence is consistent as to the fact that he fired from the gun lying in his hand and thus killed the victim Tutul. 

 8. He then submits that the learned Sessions Judge, on the basis of evidence on record, correctly found the two respondents guilty of the offence and, therefore, passed the judgment of conviction and the High Court Division committed serious error of law in reversing the said judgment, discarding the cogent evidence on record. 

 9. Mr Zainul Abedin, learned Counsel appearing on behalf of the accused respondents, has taken us through the evidence on record and other materials. 

 10. He submits that PW 1, brother of the victim, lodged first information report wherein it was stated that Moshfequr Rahman alone caught hold of the victim Tutul but the evidence has been led by the prosecution disclosing that there were other persons too who caught hold of the victim. In this respect, he has, in particular, referred to the evidence of PW 3 Sagar alias Maniruzzaman and other witnesses. 

 12. He, therefore, submits that an adverse inference is required to be drawn against the prosecution under section 114(g) of the Evidence Act. 

 13. Thereafter, he submits that departing from the first information report, a story of blasting of bomb has been imported by the prosecution in evidence which made the prosecution case more shaky. Placing the evidence of witnesses, the learned Counsel submits that from the evidence produced by the prosecution the charge could not be proved beyond doubt and so the High Court Division correctly decided the case and there is no ground for interference by this court. 

 14. We have perused the materials on record and considered the submissions made on behalf of the parties. It appears that PW 1 Liton is brother of deceased Tutul who though is not eye-witness but admits to have lodged first information report after seeing the dead body of his brother in hospital and admittedly, after the occurrence was narrated to him by PW 2 SM Hafizur Rahman, PW 3 Sagar and PW 4 SM Akil Uddin. In the said first information report PW 1 did not state that there was any blasting of bomb but in the evidence such fact has been subscribed. Moreso, it appears from the evidence that none could mention as to who blasted the bomb, if any. 

 15. It appears from the evidence of PW 1 that he deposed “হাসপাতালে আমি গিয়া আমার দুলাহ ভাই গণি ও পাড়ার অনেক লোককে দেখি” But the aforesaid dulabhai Goni, or any other person of the locality who are likely to be aware of the facts concerning the occurrence, has not been examined nor there is any explanation for their non-examination. 

 16. It further appears that the informant as PW 1 deposed that accused Moshfequr Rahman caught hold of Tutul who was killed by Ashek by firearm. But in the first information report he stated that accused Moshfeq, Mohan, Taeyab Faraji and others not named in the first information report caught  hold of Tutu I and so the High Court Division marked distinguishable departure in the evidence as to the manner of the occurrence. PW 2 SM Hafizur Rahman claiming to be eye-witness deposed that he, with others, informed the occurrence to PW 1 and in the evidence he only mentioned that he found a crowd and Moshfeq caught hold of Tutu I and thus is silent as to other persons including accused Mohan, Taeyab, etc. 

 17. He also deposed as to blasting of a bomb but he did not appear to have made any such statement to PW 1 who after hearing him lodged the first information report and, as such, the first information report is silent as to the blasting of bomb nor he deposed as to who blasted a bomb. Similarly, the evidence of PW 3 Sagar and PW 4 SM Akiluddin suffer from distinguishable departure. Other witnesses examined by the prosecution did not at all improve the prosecution case. 

 18. On consideration of the evidence on record it appears that the prosecution failed to prove the case beyond shadow of doubt and the departure, contradiction and embellishment in the prosecution case, creates doubt as to the prosecution version regarding the manner of the occurrence. In such view of the matter, the benefit of doubt goes in favour of the accused.
